note: Real Sleeper-displayed win% paired with the full game state, gathered to fit a variance-aware win probability. The point-diff-only curve in sbWinProbability cannot use these: the whole reason they were collected is that the same margin prices differently depending on how much football is left. 'left' counts STARTERS still to play or playing.

samples.notes: The pair matters more than either reading. Across the two, ours moved 1 pt while Sleeper moved 10. A player scoring on pace leaves the projected margin almost unchanged by construction -- remaining projection falls as actual rises -- so a margin-only model is frozen exactly when certainty should be climbing. Implied sigma fell from ~12 to ~8 as his game ran.

samples.margin_source: our projection for his side inverted from our 35%; the two SCORES are exact
samples.notes: Your side locked: you win iff his three COMBINE for under 3.44. Implied sigma 17.9 on ~29 pts of remaining projection.

Best sample so far -- every figure read off the screen, nothing inverted, and one player a side so each remaining projection is known exactly. Implied sigma 14.79. A flat factor needs k=0.77 here against 1.06-1.18 elsewhere, and this is the only anchor whose remaining points are mostly a QB.

samples.league: 1776 / Purple People / Dynasty is Life / Ottoman / Fantasy Football Anonymous / Doctors
samples.notes: Six near-decided matchups. Sleeper had every one at 99 (Doctors effectively 100, everyone had played) while we spread them 96 down to 65. Same root cause as the other direction: assuming an ~85 pt spread with almost no football left drags a locked game back toward a coin flip. Owner's read was that 99 is right, and it is -- with nobody left to play the projection IS the outcome.

findings: All 7 readings put us on the SAME side of 50 as Sleeper -- the margin computation is sound, only the margin->probability mapping is wrong.
We are compressed toward 50 in every single one, by up to 26 points.
Implied sigma across the 7 ranges 8.9 to 36.5. A single spread cannot produce that, so sigma has to be per-matchup.

The shipped logistic (k=0.0214 at small margins) behaves like a normal with sigma ~85 points. A full slate of 9 starters a side can only generate ~30, and one player left ~10. The curve is not merely miscalibrated, it is outside what football can produce -- which is the direct cause of everything hugging 50/50.

Best single-slope refit gets RMS error from 18.3 to 6.7 pts, but its residuals are structured: the worst (+14) is Studs and Duds, the matchup with the least football left. That is the remaining-variance signal appearing exactly where predicted.

model.form: sigma = sqrt( sum over every remaining player, both sides, of (k_pos * remaining_projection)^2 )
model.basis: Four anchors. Two have a side fully locked, so the whole distribution belongs to a known set of players. Flames is exact end to end. A single flat k fits the three skill-heavy anchors at 1.06-1.18 but needs 0.77 for the QB-heavy one; splitting QB out at 0.7 reconciles all four.
model.caveat: k_skill is not yet separated by position -- RB, WR and TE are lumped. More samples where the remaining points sit in one position would split them.

result.before: RMS 25.3 pts against the three anchors with known remaining players
